business_scope.primary_industry_name: Commercial CGI Visual Effects and 3D Character Animation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 526 of 1999 (UIAF creation and AML/CFT supervision); Law 2155 of 2021 (creation of Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales - RUB); DIAN Resolution 164 of 2021 (RUB registration procedures); Decree 830 of 2021 (AML/CFT complementary rules); SFC Circular Básica Jurídica (Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia modernized PEP and sanctions screening requirements).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Legal Existence of Foreign Entity (for corporate shareholder) or Valid Passport (for individual shareholder)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign corporate registry or notarial authority in country of origin / country-verified passport authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for Incorporation (Poder Especial para la Constitución de SAS)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public including foreign notary for optional overseas execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Name Reservation (Certificado de Homonimia / Miga Nombre) from Chamber of Commerce
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cámara de Comercio (Municipal Chamber of Commerce)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, beneficial owners, and signatories against OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated Security Council Sanctions List, Colombian domestic securities sanction lists, and contracting debarment database (Sancionados Personería Jurídica - Procuraduría). PEP status must be determined using SFC's standardized PEP definition and must trigger enhanced due diligence for high-risk PEPs irrespective of the 25% UBO threshold.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE) – Sociedad Cámara de Comercio module operated through RUES (Registro Único Empresarial y Social)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in Spanish or using the Spanish alphabet; non-Spanish script is permitted only when transliterated into Latin characters. The name must be distinguishable, morally neutral, and not confusingly similar to any existing entity in the RUES database.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within five (5) business days of rejection, the petitioner may file an administrative reconsideration (recurso de reposición) before the same Chamber of Commerce that issued the rejection. If the reconsideration is denied, an appeal (recurso de apelación) may be filed before the Superintendencia de Sociedades within five (5) additional business days. The reserved name is automatically extended for 30 days upon filing of the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is acceptable for administrative and statutory correspondence purposes in the low-risk office sector, but the S.A.S. must maintain a physical operational address in Colombia if it employs staff or handles physical infrastructure. For a commercial 3D animation studio, a virtual office is permissible for initial incorporation but a physical location for animation workstation operations is expected to satisfy commercial substance requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 5% quantified likelihood of unannounced on-site inspection during the first 12 months given the low-risk class under the unitary national risk matrix; the likelihood rises to 20% if the company opts exclusively for virtual office without a declared operational address.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff published by Superintendencia de Sociedades

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulatory fixed rate per RUES updated publication schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of incorporation deed and statutory books (Escritura de Constitución y Libros)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Maximum notary tariff established by Decree 960 of 1970 and updated Circulares Notariales

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Rejection appeal filing fee (if required) – administrative reconsideration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cost recovery fee published in the Chamber's internal tariff schedule
Market benchmark for authorized public accountant compliance preparation; no direct DIAN fee for filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fee for apostille service in the source jurisdiction

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate bylaws drafting and foreign counsel review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for S.A.S. incorporation legal package

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent / statutory domicile service for initial 12-month period
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate for low-risk office domicile and regulatory mail forwarding

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada regime), Articles 1, 5, 12-17 and 45; Código de Comercio (Decreto 410 de 1971), Articles 110-113 and 126-127; Ley 222 de 1995 (general commercial supervision framework)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá - Registro Mercantil (Commercial Registry of the Chamber of Commerce) operating through the Registro Único Empresarial (RUES) one-stop window
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation instrument) filed with the Registro Mercantil; preceded by a name pre-approval certificate and resulting in the issuance of the Matrícula Mercantil and the Chamber of Commerce incorporation certificate
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital applies under Ley 1258/2008; however, the shareholders must pay, in cash or in kind, no less than 10% of the subscribed capital at the moment of incorporation, and the balance must be paid within one year. No escrow or notarial deposit account is mandated by law; paid-in capital is evidenced by a bank deposit certificate, a sworn statement, or an appraiser's report for in-kind contributions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDING SOLE SHAREHOLDER OF [●] S.A.S. - FIRST MEETING. The undersigned shareholder, incorporating under Ley 1258 de 2008, resolves: FIRST: Approve the subscribed capital of COP [●], of which at least ten percent is paid in cash, represented by shares of equal nominal value. SECOND: Adopt the corporate bylaws as attached and establish the registered office at Calle [●], Bogotá D.C. THIRD: Appoint [●] as Legal Representative (Manager) and [●] as Alternate Manager and Compliance Officer, granting broad powers to register the company before the Chamber of Commerce and DIAN. FOURTH: Ratify all acts performed during the incorporation process and authorize issuance of the commercial registry certificate. APPROVED unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Pre-approval and Availability Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá (or territorial Chamber of Commerce) - Commercial Registry Office; online via the RUES/PAC portal at www.rues.org.co
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit one to three proposed corporate names through the online name pre-approval module (solicitud de homologación de nombre). The registry searches for identical or confusingly similar names and trademarks and issues a certificate of non-encumbrance and uniqueness of the selected name, which remains reserved for 30 calendar days.
required_dossiers: Online name request form (Formulario de solicitud de nombre)
Copy of the applicant's government-issued ID (cédula or passport)
Statement of intended corporate purpose referencing ISIC 5911 (film and audiovisual production)
Proposed corporate names (alternatives 1, 2, and 3)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for identity or similarity, file a reconsideration petition with the registry department, submit a written authorization from the prior name holder if available, or select an alternative name and resubmit immediately without forfeiting the filing queue position.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution, and Notarization of the Private Incorporation Instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary 1° del Círculo de Bogotá (optional notarization; not required unless real property is contributed) and the founding shareholders acting in private document form
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the estatutos (bylaws) in compliance with Article 5 of Ley 1258/2008, covering corporate name, registered office, precise corporate purpose (3D animation and VFX production), subscribed and paid capital, payment schedule, administration and representation clauses, statutory audit provisions, and dissolution rules. The founders execute the private document by signature; if the registry so demands, obtain a notary certification of signatures (autenticación) for the legal representative's appointment and capital contribution declarations.
required_dossiers: Draft bylaws (estatutos) in Spanish
Valid ID cards or passports of all founding shareholders
Certificate of name pre-approval from the Chamber of Commerce
Sworn capital contribution statement identifying cash or in-kind assets
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend the bylaws to cure any clauses conflicting with imperative rules of Ley 1258/2008 and the Código de Comercio, re-execute the private instrument, and obtain a new notary certification if the notary or registry raised formal objections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Filing and Issuance of the Matrícula Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá - Registro Mercantil, through the Registro Único Empresarial (RUES) electronic filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed private incorporation document, the name pre-approval certificate, and the RUES registration forms; pay the official registration tariff and the registry processing fee; record the legal representative, alternate representative, and statutory auditor (revisor fiscal only if required by law); obtain the Matrícula Mercantil certificate and the Chamber of Commerce certificate of incorporation and legal representation (certificado de existencia y representación legal).
required_dossiers: Signed private incorporation instrument in duplicate
Name pre-approval certificate
RUES registration and update forms (Formularios RUES)
Copies of identity documents of shareholders and legal representatives
Capital payment declaration or bank deposit certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Within 10 business days of receiving a deficiency notice (requerimiento), correct the identified gaps, provide missing exhibits, and resubmit; any rejection may be appealed to the Superintendencia de Sociedades under the Código de Comercio administrative procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Identification Registration (RUT and NIT) before DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) - online through the MUISCA platform at www.dian.gov.co
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the temporary Registro Único Tributario, attach the Chamber of Commerce incorporation certificate, and register the company for income tax, value-added tax, and national withholding duties. Select the applicable economic activity codes (CIUU 5911 audiovisual production and supporting services) and complete the legal representative's identification and address data; download the definitive Número de Identificación Tributaria (NIT) certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and legal representation from the Chamber of Commerce
Legal representative's valid ID
Temporary RUT application form (pre-RUT)
Proof of registered office address (lease or authorization letter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any DIAN requerimiento within the statutory one-month term, correct the tax classification or address data, and update the RUT record electronically; request an extension if additional corporate documentation is needed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Corporate Bank Account and Payment of Paid-in Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Any commercial bank authorized by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia (e.g., Bancolombia, Banco de Bogotá, Davivienda)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate savings or checking account in the name of the S.A.S. and deposit no less than 10% of the subscribed capital, or the entire amount if the one-year payment term is shortened. Obtain the bank's certificate of deposit or account statement reflecting the capital credit and preserve it as evidence of the paid-in capital requirement; the funds may be used immediately for incorporation expenses and operating needs.
required_dossiers: Cámara de Comercio certificate of existence and legal representation
NIT / RUT certificate
Corporate bylaws and first board resolution
Valid ID of the legal representative and authorized signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or registry questions the paid-in capital evidence, obtain a certified capital deposit certificate from the bank or a notary-certified sworn statement from the shareholder, and resubmit the documentation to the requesting party.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal and Ancillary Operation Registrations (ICA, Fire Safety, and Establishment Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía Mayor de Bogotá / Secretaría Distrital de Hacienda (Industria y Comercio tax and commercial establishment registration) and Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos de Bogotá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company in the municipal Industria y Comercio (ICA) tax roll, file the corresponding annual declaration forms, and register the commercial establishment (3D animation production office) with the municipal authority. Request the fire safety inspection for the leased premises, obtain the Certificado de Condiciones de Seguridad contra Incendios, and register the workplace with the occupational risk insurer (ARL) and the Ministerio del Trabajo for workplace safety clearance.
required_dossiers: RUT and NIT certificates
Matrícula Mercantil certificate
Lease contract (contrato de arrendamiento) or title deed of the premises
ICA registration form and annual declaration template
Fire safety inspection application and building occupancy permit (certificado de uso de suelo compatible with office use)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For municipal rejections, correct the land-use certificate or zoning documents and resubmit; for fire safety deficiencies, remedy the identified hazards (extinguishers, signage, emergency exits) within the inspection deadline and schedule a re-inspection; appeal tax assessments to the Secretaría Distrital de Hacienda within the statutory term.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial licensing board authorization is required for CGI and 3D character animation production under Colombian law; the only relevant authorities are the Alcaldía Municipal / Secretaría Distrital de Hacienda for commercial establishment registration, the Curaduría Urbana for land-use and occupancy permits, and the Ministerio de Tecnologías de la Información y las Comunicaciones (MINTIC) only if broadcasting or telecommunications services are added to the corporate purpose.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registro de Establecimiento Comercial and Certificado de Condiciones de Seguridad contra Incendios (commercial operation registration, which is optional in the strict licensing sense but mandatory as a municipal regulatory formality)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) - Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from EIA: office-based audiovisual and animation production generates no significant environmental impact and is not listed in Decree 1076/2015 licensing categories; only an administrative environmental registration may be requested if the operation expands to physical sets, heavy diesel generators, or large-format printing.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with Decreto 1076/2015 (Código de Recursos Naturales): office wastewater must discharge exclusively to the municipal sewerage system under local limits (DOB and COD within municipal thresholds); no VOC or atmospheric emission thresholds apply to CGI workstation processes, but any exhaust from emergency generators must meet local air quality limits; electronic waste (computers, GPUs, batteries) must be handed to licensed recyclers and hazardous waste managers under Resolución 1326/2017 and Decreto 4741/2005.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Requires the Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos fire safety certification (Certificado de Condiciones de Seguridad contra Incendios) covering fire extinguishers, evacuation signage and exit capacity; structural load validation by the Curaduría Urbana or a licensed engineer for tenant improvements and heavy equipment racks; and mandatory registration of the workplace with the Administradora de Riesgos Laborales (ARL) plus an occupational health and safety program (SG-SST) in accordance with Decreto 1072/2015 and Resolución 0312/2019.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) - the unified Colombian national tax and customs authority; official digital portal: https://www.dian.gov.co (Sede Electrónica).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident-owned Colombian S.A.S. must: (1) complete incorporation before the municipal Cámara de Comercio with notarised by-laws and the appointment of a Colombian legal representative; (2) obtain the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) and register in the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) through DIAN's Sede Electrónica, with the assistance of a local certified public accountant; (3) declare in the RUT the status of IVA-responsible, income-tax resident, exporter-of-services and holder of a foreign-exchange reintegration account; (4) procure the DIAN digital signature (firma electrónica) through an authorised certification provider; and (5) activate DIAN-approved electronic invoicing credentials (CUFE capability) before issuing any sales invoice. The full procedure is executable online and is usually completed within two to five business days after the chamber of commerce registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia does not provide a US-style check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election. The relevant statutory elections are: (a) an annual, binding election to join the Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE) where the S.A.S.'s prior-year gross income remains within the UVT-indexed cap; SIMPLE substitutes the ordinary corporate income tax and, for qualifying service income, replaces VAT collection with progressive combined rates of 1.4% to 14.5%; (b) the default classification as an ordinary IVA-responsible and entity-level CIT taxpayer (35% standard rate) for all other S.A.S. entities; (c) eligibility to apply for 'Gran Contribuyente' status, a DIAN administrative classification based on turnover that centralises clearance and shortens VAT refund cycles; and (d) a protective disclosure obligation, not an election, with respect to hybrid mismatch arrangements, which are statutorily disallowed under BEPS Action 2.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis turnover threshold exists for VAT registration: every S.A.S. performing taxable services in Colombia must register as IVA-responsible in the RUT regardless of revenue level. The only UVT-indexed threshold relevant to indirect taxation is the annual ceiling for the SIMPLE combined regime (80,000-100,000 UVT of gross income for service providers, approximately COP 4.0-5.0 billion for tax years 2024-2025), which conditions the combined-regime election and does not waive the RUT/IVA registration duty.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Colombia mandates real-time fiscal clearance of all electronic invoices (Facturación Electrónica). Under DIAN Resolution No. 000165 of 2023, sales invoices must be transmitted as XML to DIAN Web Services or through an authorised technology provider (ADP) for immediate validation; DIAN assigns the final sequential number and the unique CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) digital stamp, and only after clearance may the invoice be delivered to the client. The printable PDF must contain the QR code validated by DIAN. Export invoices for CGI, VFX and 3D animation deliverables must use the export-of-services transaction code and state the 0% VAT basis. The same infrastructure requires real-time transmission of the electronic support document (documento soporte) for B2B acquisitions from non-obligated parties. Failure to e-invoice suspends VAT input credits, blocks export zero-rating, and triggers penalties under Article 652-14 of the Tax Code.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% IVA export treatment for commercial 3D animation, CGI and VFX services is available under Article 481, literal c), of the Colombian Tax Code as developed by Decree 1625 of 2016, provided that: (i) the service is rendered to a recipient that has no tax residence or permanent establishment in Colombia; (ii) the animation, VFX plates, rigs, render files and digital assets are effectively used, enjoyed or commercially exploited outside Colombian territory; (iii) the Colombian S.A.S. is the contractual supplier of the finished deliverables to the foreign production studio; and (iv) the consideration is payable in foreign currency by a non-resident entity. Digital delivery to foreign licensees qualifies as an export of services, and the S.A.S. may claim monthly refunds of pre-export input VAT attributable to the zero-rated transactions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Signed commercial export contract with the foreign production company identifying the animation/VFX deliverables, the foreign licensee or end-client and the effective foreign exploitation clause
DIAN-cleared electronic invoice issued in the exporter's name bearing the CUFE and stating the 0% VAT (export) basis and the applicable customs/service tariff nomenclature
Electronic export-of-services declaration (Declaración de Exportación de Servicios) transmitted through DIAN's export platform, in PDF/XML accompanied by the DIAN acknowledgement receipt
Foreign-currency inflow certificate (certificado de reintegro cambiario / declaración de cambio) issued by the Colombian intermediary bank evidencing inbound remittance of the export proceeds
Sworn statement or confirmation letter signed by the foreign client certifying that the animation is exploited outside Colombia, plus asset delivery manifests for licensed IP and source files
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN may audit export zero-rating substantiation and the foreign-currency reintegration trail. If the 0% VAT treatment is disallowed, the full 19% IVA is assessed retroactively from the applicable tax period, plus default interest (currently indexed in the range of 20-30% annual) and the inexactity penalty under Article 648 of the Tax Code - generally 100% of the assessed tax, increased to 160% where deliberate fraud is proven. Exporters claiming input VAT refunds remain subject to a 24-month audit look-back; improper refunds are clawed back with a 100% surcharge under Article 670 of the Tax Code and potential suspension of the RUT exporter status. Aggravated conduct, including falsified reintegration certificates or sham foreign clients, incurs customs-related criminal sanctions under Law 1762 of 2015, with fines of up to 300% of the export value and imprisonment of four to nine years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia), acting through its Board of Directors and foreign exchange office, with supervisory support from the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia and administrative enforcement coordination with the Ministerio de Hacienda y Crédito Público and the DIAN.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates a managed floating COP/USD regime administered through the regulated mercado cambiario. Current-account transactions such as cross-border services, royalty payments, trade settlements, and interest are convertible through authorized intermediaries provided the corresponding foreign-exchange declaration is completed. Capital-account transactions require the foreign investment to be registered with Banco de la República through a Colombian bank in order to secure lawful repatriation rights for capital, dividends, and capital gains. There is no absolute prohibition on profit remittance, but remittance depends on registered foreign investment, audited financial statements evidencing distributable earnings, and satisfaction of Colombian withholding taxes. The practical hurdle is documentary: banks will not process the FX operation without a complete Form 4 or equivalent foreign-investment declaration, so the S.A.S. must maintain a clean share subscription paper trail and the foreign investor’s source-of-funds evidence.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters of goods and services must channel 100% of export proceeds into the Colombian regulated foreign-exchange market through an authorized intermediary within the maximum timelines set by Banco de la República, generally up to six months from the export date for goods and from the contractual payment due date for services unless a longer bank-authorized payment term applies. The mandated surrender entry does not automatically require immediate conversion to COP: proceeds may be retained in a foreign-currency account at a local authorized bank or in a compensation account previously registered with Banco de la República. If the exporter needs to make peso disbursements, the conversion must be settled through an authorized intermediary at the negotiated market exchange rate and supported by the relevant foreign-exchange declaration, commercial invoice, contract, and customs or service-delivery evidence.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital electronic-money institutions such as Wise B2B are rated Medium for ancillary disbursements, contractor payments, and low-value FX conversion, but Low as a substitute for the local Colombian banking and foreign-exchange system. They are not authorized foreign-exchange intermediaries under Colombian law and cannot satisfy the statutory channeling of export proceeds, the registration of foreign investment, or the filing of currency declarations with Banco de la República. Wise B2B is therefore legally usable only for non-statutory treasury flows or as a payment convenience layer, provided the Colombian S.A.S. maintains its substantive receipts, capital injection, tax payments, and dividend repatriation through a licensed local bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, a non-resident director or beneficial owner of the S.A.S. will need to appear physically in Colombia or appoint a Colombian attorney-in-fact with a notarized and apostilled power of attorney. Colombian banks apply Sarlaft-based customer due diligence and routinely require an AML interview for the legal representative and direct or beneficial owners. Pure remote account opening is emerging through digital onboarding channels, but for a newly incorporated S.A.S. with foreign shareholders the banks usually require at least one in-person interview, original passport, company incorporation certificate from the Cámara de Comercio, NIT certificate, and a valid representation certificate. Failure to satisfy the physical or notarial authentication step is the most common reason for delayed onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders and foreign directors without Colombian identity documents, credit history, or local economic footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of existence and legal representation from Cámara de Comercio; certified constitutional documents and share registry; Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUB) filing; passport copies and proof of foreign address for each shareholder and director; notarized and apostilled power of attorney; curriculum vitae and professional references for the animation business; beneficial-ownership organizational chart; source-of-funds bank statements for at least the prior 12 months; and a written declaration of lawful origin of capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming capital contribution from an offshore entity or a jurisdiction perceived as a tax haven or high-risk shell-company jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed foreign-investment share subscription agreement; corporate board resolution of the investor authorizing the capital contribution; audited or accountant-reviewed financial statements of the investor; tax residence certificate; evidence of the investor’s real economic activity; legal opinion from a foreign counsel confirming entity existence and powers; final beneficial-owner chain; commercial business plan showing the S.A.S. CGI and 3D animation activities; and a formal rationale for the Colombian operating entity as a near-shore delivery hub.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions screening hits, PEP status, or adverse media involving a shareholder, director, or ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent sanctions-screening report; PEP declaration and source-of-wealth statement; official criminal background certificates from all countries of residence; corporate resolutions clarifying the transaction; independent enhanced-due-diligence report; evidence of the lawful origin of funds; and a written AML compliance decision approved by the Colombian bank’s compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transaction profile mismatch in which incoming client wires from foreign production studios do not match the declared CGI/VFX business activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial contracts with animation studios and producers; detailed invoices and statements of work; delivery and acceptance certificates for 3D assets, sequences, or final renders; project breakdown showing ISIC 5911 and NAICS 512110 activity; internal production logs and render metadata; bank source-of-funds declarations; and reconciliation between the corporate treasury ledger and the foreign-exchange declarations filed with Banco de la República.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign capital into the Colombian S.A.S. should be routed exclusively by SWIFT MT103 from the direct non-resident investor’s bank to the S.A.S. operating account at an authorized Colombian bank. The beneficiary field must show the S.A.S. legal name and NIT, and the payment purpose in field 70 should state foreign direct investment for subscription of shares. The receiving bank will prepare the inward foreign-investment declaration with Banco de la República, convert the USD to COP where appropriate, and verify the identity of the remitting investor against the registered share registry. The company must support the wire with notarized minutes of capital subscription, a copy of the investor’s constitutional documents, tax residency proof, ultimate beneficial owner information, and the source of funds. Unregulated digital EMI transfers must not be used for capital injection because they cannot produce the regulated FX declaration required for lawful future dividend remittance or capital repatriation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Payments to foreign animation subcontractors, rendering farms, licensing agents, cloud providers, voice talent, and technology vendors should be effected through SWIFT MT103 from the local Colombian bank after the corresponding foreign-exchange declaration for services has been prepared. MT202 may be used for correspondent interbank cover where required. For physical production deliverables crossing customs, such as proprietary hardware or final media masters, documentary settlement through a commercial letter of credit can be used, with the bank requiring invoices, airway bills or bills of lading, certificates of inspection, and evidence of export/import compliance. For pure digital services, the commercial letter of credit is inappropriate; the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 supported by a service contract, invoice, statement of work, and proof of service delivery. The treasury function must map every outbound payment to a declared basis such as service import, royalty remittance, capital account transfer, or repayment of registered foreign debt.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright COP/USD deliverable forward contracts executed with a Banco de la República authorized commercial bank, provided there is a documented underlying commercial, investment, or trade exposure.

Non-deliverable forward contracts (NDFs) on COP/USD entered into with an authorized local bank or an eligible international bank, used when COP settlement is operationally inconvenient or forward liquidity is unavailable in the local market.

COP/USD cross-currency swaps covering long-term USD-denominated capital structures or material foreign cash-flow mismatches, executed through regulated financial institutions and, where required, declared or registered with Banco de la República.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late surcharge of 2% monthly computed on the applicable fee; administrative fines up to 17 UVT per infraction; continued non-renewal for two consecutive years triggers administrative strike-off of the commercial registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March, accompanied by the renewal and a certificate of the approval by the general shareholders' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may result in fines by the Superintendencia de Sociedades and inability to carry out certain legal procedures; the Chamber of Commerce may refuse to issue a certificate of legal existence while the filing is pending.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually during August-September; exact due date assigned by the last digit of the NIT
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 5% of the tax due, increasing to 10% after three months, plus monthly interest on penalties; persistent delinquency may lead to asset seizure and criminal liability for tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Update (Actualización de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the annual renewal deadline, ordinarily by 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines by the Chamber of Commerce for non-compliance; the company may be barred from obtaining certificates and registration renewals until the information is validly submitted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Shareholders' Meeting Approval of Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate Minute Book (internal, not filed with an external authority)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be held by 31 March following the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct financial sanction, but failure to hold the meeting and approve accounts may invalidate the financial statement filing and expose the company to shareholder claims and regulatory fines.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory Revisor Fiscal (statutory auditor) is required when total assets exceed 5,000 UVT (approx. COP 235 million) or gross income exceeds 3,000 UVT in the preceding fiscal year; also mandatory if provided by the bylaws or the general shareholders' meeting.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB and adopted in Colombia (NIC/NIIF Group 1 full IFRS or Group 2 SME IFRS, as defined by Decree 2420 of 2015).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A confirmation of the final beneficiaries must be submitted annually through the 'Beneficiario Final' module of the Chamber of Commerce. Each direct or indirect shareholding transfer in the company triggers an immediate register update and a revision of the beneficial ownership statement. The company must compare the updated shareholder registry against the prior UBO declaration and file the revised report within one month after the annual renewal, or sooner if a transfer occurs.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Registro de Junta Directiva)
Register of Beneficial Owners (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,000 - 3,000 per year (if compulsory audit thresholds are met)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% (national corporate income tax, inclusive of the surtax abolished for general taxpayers; note that a 3% surtax applies to certain specified taxable income amounts above COP 0 under Law 2277 of 2022, effectively raising the marginal headline rate to up to 38% for large taxpayers with taxable income exceeding COP 0 as defined)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general territorial tax holiday. The 'Orange Economy' regime (Law 1955 of 2019, Article 176) historically provided a reduced income tax rate of 26% for new creative digital and animation companies located in specified excluded zones, but the benefit required prior registration with the CONPES committee and has been restricted and effectively dormant for new entrants. Standard incentives include: (a) a 25% corporate income tax deduction for investments in research, technological development, and innovation approved by the National Council for Science, Technology and Innovation; (b) VAT exemption on the export of animation services and related digital services; (c) accelerated depreciation for fixed assets certified as environmentally beneficial or linked to animation production technology; (d) tax credit for VAT paid on the import of machinery and equipment for qualified productive service activities, capped at 4% of the FOB value; (e) no foreign tax credit limitation beyond the general rule under Article 254 of the Tax Code, allowing a credit for foreign income taxes paid up to the Colombian tax attributable to that foreign-source income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 210 (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios or 'Renta' for legal entities) filed through the Dian electronic filing portal 'Sí@Web' (https://www.dian.gov.co). Mandatory electronic signature using a valid Digital Certificate. Aggregated annual return covering income, complementary taxes, and the presumptive income minimum (renta presuntiva).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal year aligns with calendar year in Colombia; no alternative fiscal year election for tax purposes except for special situations approved by the tax authority).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline for the previous taxable year (ending 31 December) is scheduled in nine chronological groups based on the last two digits of the taxpayer's NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria), generally between 18 March and 12 April of the following year. Tax payment installments are due at the same deadline. No extension is available for the corporate income tax return beyond the published DIAN calendar. For taxpayers under the simplified tax regime (Régimen Simple de Tributación) a different consolidated form applies, but an S.A.S. engaged in commercial animation retains the ordinary regime unless an opt-in election was made.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company NIT, full legal name, registered address, economic activity code (CIIU, mandatory 6-digit code; for animation and VFX production, use 5911 'Actividades de producción de películas cinematográficas, videos, programas, publicidad y animación' — verify if DIAN subclassification 591130 applies for computer-generated animation).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not entered on this box; the form relates to the Colombian S.A.S. itself. If the S.A.S. is controlled by a non-resident, include the foreign parent's name in the special disclosure annex for related-party transactions only when transfer pricing thresholds are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 210 - Box 34 (Ingresos brutos operacionales del exterior)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from the rendering of animation and 3D rendering services to non-resident clients, including contracts executed abroad with effective use and enjoyment outside Colombia. In Colombia taxation is territorial (source-based, not worldwide; Article 24 of the Tax Code).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the Colombian entity reports these amounts. Export services are generally Colombian-source if exploited in Colombia; for services, source is determined by where the service is performed, so render-farm production executed in Colombia but delivered to a foreign client requires careful technical analysis. Most animation contracts are deemed Colombian-source because the underlying service and productive activity occurs inside Colombia; nevertheless, they may still enjoy VAT exemption under the export of services regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct production costs, including salaries of 3D animators, modelers, riggers, lighting artists, software license fees, amortization of in-house CGI libraries, and cloud rendering infrastructure costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: When a non-resident shareholder supplies intangibles (proprietary 3D engines, character pipelines), the S.A.S. must deduct amortization or royalties only if evidenced by contract, remittance backup, and withholding tax certificates. No deduction is allowed without proper transfer pricing documentation if the counterparty is a related party.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 210 - Box 45 (Deducciones especiales - inversiones en desarrollo tecnológico)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction at 25% of investments in qualified research, technological development, and innovation, as certified by the Ministry of Science, Technology, and Innovation. Animation R&D involving new rendering algorithms, AI-assisted animation, and procedural generation may qualify.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenditures incurred in Colombia qualify; payments to foreign related parties for R&D are generally not eligible for this incentive unless the project is approved and performed materially in Colombia with local certified personnel.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Presumptive income floor: a minimum taxable income equal to 0% of the tax basis of net equity (but subject to transitional rules under Law 2277/2022: for tax year 2023, 0.5% of net equity; for 2024, 0% and thereafter eliminated for most taxpayers), or 3.5% of the tax basis of net equity for those subject to the 15% minimum tax regime. For an animation S.A.S. with high equity but low revenue in an early production phase, this may invoke a minimum taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders' contributed capital is included in net equity; excess equity from unpaid capital subscriptions (capital suscrito no pagado) is included unless the subscription has a firm maturities schedule and has been paid within the statutory period. An animation S.A.S. with US-invested equity and delayed first contract should monitor this risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 210 - Box 56 (Impuesto a cargo / contribución al Fondo de Cine)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The animation company may be subject to the film development contribution (Cuota para el Desarrollo Cinematográfico) if directly engaged in feature film production, to be disclosed separately, not in the income tax calculation; for commercial 3D animation produced exclusively for advertising or VFX under contract, the quota typically does not apply. Box 56 records the mandatory corporate income tax calculated at the statutory rate (after the orange economy preferential rate if previously granted).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If profits are to be distributed, the return must compute the income tax as a legal entity; no consolidation with foreign shareholders is permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 210 - Box 64 (Anticipo al impuesto de renta)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance tax installment calculated from the prior year's income tax liability: for the 2024 filing season, entities with a prior-year tax liability of COP 0 or below $3,300,000 (about USD 1,000) are exempt; otherwise, the advance equals 100% of the income tax liability minus withholdings that are recoverable, net of certain credits. This is an additional collectible cash burden.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders should plan cash flow; the S.A.S. must self-assess this advance even if profit repatriation to the foreign parent is the strategy.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 210 - Box 70 (Retenciones en la fuente que le practicaron)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Creditable withholding taxes withheld by Colombian clients on domestic invoices, including the 2.5% general withholding on services and honoraria and the 6.375% special withholding on service company income when applicable. For export-flagged services, invoice them with the export exclusion, and provide valid export service certificates, so no withholding is applied at the local client.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For outbound payments (e.g., SaaS licenses from foreign platforms), the S.A.S. must self-withhold the corresponding withholding tax on the payment to the foreign vendor (generally 15% on royalty-like services) and report it in Annex 1, but the same withholding is a recoupable credit only if the contract is a technical or software service with the effective exploitation in Colombia.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form 210 - Box 90 (Total contribuciones a cargo / total a pagar)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sum of corporate income tax plus the net of the advance tax, less credits, withholdings, and any excess advance from prior years. The final amount must be paid via DIAN electronic payment (Banco de la República codes). A Colombian digital animation S.A.S. with a COP zero income but high expenses will still owe minimum advance and potentially the presumptive floor discussed above.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must ensure remittances for working capital are formally capitalized either as equity or as loans registered in the national exchange (Banco de la República) to avoid thin capitalization disallowance of interest under Article 118-1 (excess leverage at a D/E ratio above 3:1).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: (a) 5% of the tax due per month or fraction of month of delay, capped at 100% of the tax due, with a minimum of COP 1,000,000 (about USD 250) for no-tax returns; (b) if filing is submitted within one year of the statutory deadline and the return shows no tax due from the taxpayer's own determination, a minimum penalty of COP 2,000,000 applies; (c) if the return is not filed within one year, DIAN will impose an assessment based on its presumed determination, and the penalty increases to 10% per month up to 200% of the assessed tax; (d) a 20% reduction is available if the taxpayer files late voluntarily before any DIAN requirement. Daily interest for underpayment of tax is calculated at the prevailing annual usury-linked interest rate (currently around 25.6% effective annual), applied on the revised tax assessment. For an S.A.S. with no operations but required to file (a mandatory requirement if it exists at year-end), failure to file even with a zero result triggers a minimum penalty of COP 0 optional for zero filers, but local practice requires a formal 'no income' filing to avoid a presumed assessment. Directors who knowingly sign a false return may be sanctioned under Articles 433–435 of the Tax Code with imprisonment of 2 to 8 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 7.5% on non-resident recipients (dividend withholding tax). The statutory structure is: (i) corporate income tax has already been levied at the S.A.S. level; (ii) dividends paid from non-taxable or already-taxed profits to non-residents trigger an additional 7.5% withholding when paid out of 'net taxable income' that was subject to the general corporate rate (Article 245, Tax Code); (iii) for non-resident individuals and entities, if the profit has been taxed, the rate is 7.5%; if paid from tax-exempt income, the rate is 15%; but for most commercial animation earnings, the 7.5% is the effective final statutory rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Colombia's tax treaty network includes Spain, Canada, Mexico, South Korea, Chile, Switzerland, Czech Republic, Portugal, UK, France, India, Japan, Germany, Netherlands, Italy, UAE, Brazil (signed, not yet fully effective for all provinces), and the Andean Community Decision 578 (partial). For a US-based animation S.A.S., if the shareholder is in the US, no US-Colombia DTA exists, so the statutory 7.5% dividend rate applies; for UK, French, German, or Dutch holding companies, the DTA may reduce the rate. The application protocol for treaty relief: (a) the Colombian S.A.S. withholds the statutory 7.5%; (b) the non-resident must obtain a Colombian 'Autorización de aplicación de beneficios de convenio' by submitting a Certificate of Tax Residency issued by the relevant foreign tax authority and a completed Form 140 or electronic form via 'Módulo de Beneficios de Convenios' in the DIAN portal before or at the moment of the dividend distribution; (c) the S.A.S. must record the reduced rate only if the DIAN has previously approved the certificate, otherwise must withhold at the statutory rate and the non-resident may file a refund claim through a Colombian tax attorney; (d) the TRC must state the fiscal residence and clearly identify the latter clause on 'beneficial ownership'; a certificate obtained retroactively is generally not accepted for an already distributed dividend, so retrospective refund proceedings are expensive and liability-prone.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for IP (including licensed 3D animation software, character copyrights, and patented CGI processes): statutory withholding rate 15% for resident beneficiaries; for non-residents, 33% is withheld on the gross amount deemed Colombian-source if paid by a Colombian resident for use in Colombia, unless reduced by a DTA; the standard treaty rate for royalties ranges from 0%–10% (e.g., Mexico 10%, Chile 10%, Portugal 5%, Switzerland 5% if the beneficiary is the beneficial owner and specific requirements). Interest paid to a non-resident financial institution: statutory 15% on gross if the creditor is a bank or financial entity; for non-financial related-party interest, 15%; under DTA protocols, interest rates are typically 0%–10% (Spain 10%, UK 10% under UKDTA), but eligibility requires fulfillment of the LOB or beneficial ownership tests in each DTA. Caution: interest remittances to a related non-resident are recharacterized if the local S.A.S. is undercapitalized (D/E ratio > 3:1) – see transfer pricing thin capitalization rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory documentation for the fiscal year is required if the taxpayer: (a) conducts transactions vis-à-vis related parties abroad (including a foreign parent and any sub-licensed intangibles) and (b) meets either: gross assets exceeding COP 150,000 UVT (approximately COP 150,000 * 47,065 = COP 7,059,750,000, about USD 1.75 million as of 2025 – but verify annually), or gross income exceeding COP 100,000 UVT (approximately COP 4,706,500,000, about USD 1.16 million), or (c) in all cases the taxpayer must file an annual transfer-pricing informative return (Form 120, 'Información de Operaciones con Vinculados') if it has transactions with related parties and meets the medium taxpayer size thresholds: gross income above COP 100,000 UVT (COP 4,706.5 million) or gross assets above COP 100,000 UVT. Additionally, as a 'taxpayer without TP obligation' but with a foreign shareholder, the S.A.S. must file the Country-by-Country declaration if the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds COP 87 billion. For a smaller US-owned animation S.A.S., the TP return is unlikely to be triggered on the asset or income thresholds unless the studio ramps up quickly, but benchmarking against the local commercial rule is mandatory because non-resident parents often understate service fees; a conservative standard is to prepare a simplified comparability analysis whenever any cross-border related transaction exists.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP (Comparable Uncontrolled Price): for export of finished animation projects to the foreign parent, if the parent resells to end clients, an internal CUP based on prices charged to independent distributors or a direct comparable CUP is preferred.
Resale Price Method: for a S.A.S. that acts as a low-risk production arm selling animation deliverables to a foreign principal; gross margin earned must align with local independent resellers.

Cost Plus Method: most suitable for an animation/VFX service provider paid on a cost-plus basis (industry margins observed by Colombian TP comparables in creative services generally range from 8%–15% net, but the statutory safe harbor is not law). The S.A.S. should document its actual full-cost allocation, excluding non-operating FX effects, and apply a mark-up consistent with the 'commercial animation and post-production services' comparables.

TNMM (Transactional Net Margin Method): the dominant methodology for the industry; use net profit on total costs (Berry ratio) or operating margin on revenues, with robust public databases of Latin American creative service companies; a Berry ratio in the range of 1.10–1.30 is often accepted for low-risk service providers with no significant IP ownership, but in Colombia a markup over total operating expenses of 10%–18% is commonly reviewed.

Profit Split Method: applicable where both the Colombian S.A.S. and the foreign parent contribute unique intangibles and assume risks (e.g., the Colombian studio owns a proprietary animation rigging library and the parent owns marketing client relationships); in such cases, a profit split based on R&D costs or capital employed is defensible, but DIAN scrutiny is high, and the S.A.S. should document the DEMPE functions to avoid the parent being deemed the sole owner.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not maintain a general Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime comparable to the UAE or Cyprus. However, the general anti-avoidance rule under Article 869-1 of the Tax Code allows DIAN to disregard legal forms lacking economic substance, and the 're-characterization of transactions with related parties' is used to reclassify payments as dividends. For the S.A.S. engaged in animation, the substance doctrine manifests in: (a) adequate payroll, physical render-farm presence, and actual artistic management in Colombian territory; (b) if the S.A.S. is a pure invoice-passer for services actually performed by non-resident contractors, DIAN will likely treat all income as taxable without the offsetting expenses, or reclassify the profit allocation to the foreign parent; (c) For claiming the benefit of the preferential 'naranja' regime or VAT export exemption, DIAN applies a formal substance test – the S.A.S. must prove technical staff physically present in Colombia and invoices remitted from Colombian infrastructure; (d) The application of DTA benefits for dividends requires substantive rather than formal beneficial ownership (treaty shopping) – if the foreign parent is an intermediate holding with no substance in its residence state, DIAN may deny treaty relief despite a pending treaty, citing the Anti-Tax Treaty Shopping rules under Law 1819 of 2016, Article 124.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False or insufficient filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Ukrainian-style deliberate under-reporting of revenues from foreign 3D animation contracts, use of shell invoicing from a related foreign 'animation licensing' entity that is actually a conduit with no staff, or exclusion of taxable export income from the Form 210 while retaining the funds in the foreign parent account.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment of 2 to 8 years for individuals (Article 426 Tax Code). The S.A.S. faces: (a) collection of the omitted tax; (b) penalty equal to 100% of the amount omitted (or 200% if assets are hidden); (c) daily interest; (d) a criminal fine of up to COP 1,500 million for the legal entity; (e) publication of the taxpayer's name in DIAN's insolvent-taxpayer list. If the omission exceeds COP 250,000,000 (about USD 62,600), the sanction is aggravated to 8 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Director and legal representative are jointly and severally liable for the tax debt if they had knowledge of the under-reporting and approved the return (Article 794/795 of the Tax Code). Additionally, under the Colombian Criminal Code (Law 599/2000, Article 413), a representative who orders, authorizes, or tolerates false tax declarations faces imprisonment, loss of professional license, and travel-ban (prohibition to leave Colombia by DIAN order under Article 839-3). Civil restitution to the treasury includes the tax, penalty, and updated interest; a director may be barred from holding board positions in any Colombian company for up to 10 years. But for the typical US entrepreneur, the more immediate risk is a freeze on personal assets in Colombia and inability to obtain a Colombian residence visa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure and Mis-pricing of cross-border services
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Missing the mandatory transfer-pricing return (Form 120) when thresholds are met, or failure to prepare the Local File / Master File before the annual filing date, or pricing intercompany animation license fees at an artificial high price to strip profits (e.g., paying 90% of the gross margin to the parent for use of a generic animation software pipeline that is not unique).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: If the taxpayer meets the TP documentation obligation but does not file Form 120, the penalty is COP 40,000,000 (about USD 10,000) per month of delay (suspended after 24 months). If the TP return and Local File are not prepared and submitted, DIAN may: (a) adjust the net income upward to the arm's length result; (b) apply a penalty of 10% to 200% of the difference between the reported and adjusted taxable income; (c) interest at 25%+ annual; (d) disallow the deductions and re-classify the excess payment as a dividend deemed distribution for the foreign shareholder, triggering the 7.5% dividend withholding plus penalties. If the S.A.S. has a loss but the transfer pricing adjustment eliminates the loss, the advance tax and presumptive tax clauses also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign a false transfer pricing certification (the sworn statement in Form 120) are personally liable for the penalty (the general penalty of 5% of underlying tax). In egregious cases where the mispricing has a criminal character (e.g., creation of a nominal foreign licensor with no actual economic activity), the director may receive a 4-year imprisonment under the fraudulent-evasion doctrine. In practice, DIAN includes personal liability statements in any formal assessment, and if the company becomes insolvent, the director receives a personal assessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Lack of Economic Substance (tax haven misuse)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Colombian S.A.S. as a subordinate shell for a foreign tax-optimized group, maintaining minimal staff in Colombia, outsourcing all the artistic production to contractors outside Colombia while claiming Colombian-source expenses and tax credits, or claiming a Colombian residence certificate while the actual control and management are exercised in a tax-haven parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 869-1 of the Tax Code, the transaction is recharacterized, all tax benefits granted to the S.A.S. are reversed, and the S.A.S. is classified as a 'sociedad de fachada' if it lacks real operations. Consequences: (a) all revenues are assigned to the actual foreign operator, and Colombian tax at 35% is assessed with penalties; (b) VAT on the local digital services becomes payable if the S.A.S. is deemed not to be the actual exporter, so the statutory 19% VAT will be assessed on the full invoice; (c) the S.A.S. may be disqualified as a legitimate exporter; (d) the foreign parent could be additionally assessed under the concept of 'permanent establishment in Colombia' and subject to the 6.3% branch remittance tax; (e) administrative sanctions under Law 1121/2006 for international exchange fraud if remittances were misreported to the central bank.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who signs the 'export service certificate' for a transaction the company does not actually perform incurs fraud liability. Additional risk arises under the anti-money-laundering framework (Law 526/2018) if the 'stripped profits' are repatriated disguised as non-trade payments; directors may face money-laundering charges (law 599/2000, Article 323) with 10 to 30 years of imprisonment. Civil liability extends to compensation for nonexistent VAT export credits, which are considered the direct patrimony of the state.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and International Exchange (FX) Infractions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving payments for the 3D animation services via unauthorized or unreported foreign currency accounts (e.g., using a US or Singapore Wise/B2B account as an undeclared collection channel), failing to register the null use of the free exchange regime under the Banco de la República regulations (Decreto 1368/2016 requires all foreign-currency collections for services to be channeled or at least reported in the 'Declaración de Cambio' if the amount exceeds USD 10,000 per month, or if the payment is not from an approved intermediary, the appropriate customs declaration), or issuing anticipos (prepayments) from the foreign client that are not duly reported.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The exchange violation carries the penalty of (a) confiscation of the foreign currency equivalent not reported; (b) a fine up to 200% of the unreported amount if the capital is unrepatriated; (c) suspension from exporting privileges for up to 5 years; additionally, the use of an unregistered and unreported Wise account can trigger the Colombian Statute of Exchange Control (Law 9 of 1991), with penalties calculated as 100% of the value of the foreign currency not surrendered when the exporter is subject to surrender obligations (the service exporter is generally exempt from mandatory surrender but must still report). Criminal AMPI risk: under the Criminal Statute (Law 526), if the unreported inflow is associated with an act of tax evasion, a director faces 8 to 15 years; for a low-risk standard animation company, the infraction usually remains administrative unless the tax evasion overlay exists.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Banco de la República and DIAN can jointly impose civil sanctions on the legal representative (the natural person signing the export declaration). If the foreign exchange remains abroad without declaration, the director becomes the addressee of the penalty, and a travel ban can be issued by DIAN (Article 839-3 of the Tax Code has no exception for non-resident directors). If the director is a non-resident and a Colombian S.A.S. is the only asset, the travel ban effectively traps the director if he or she enters Colombia for a client meeting.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Attempting to repatriate profits to the foreign shareholder disguised as 'cost reimbursement', 'management fees', or 'non-interest bearing shareholder loans' to avoid the 7.5% dividend withholding tax, or refusing to withhold the 7.5% and then sending a wire to the US parent as a 'loan repayment' without the documentation required by DIAN; also, structuring royalties as 'technical services' with 15% instead of 33% withholding when the service is not genuinely technical or is in fact a license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN recharacterization triggers: (a) the assessed tax of 7.5% or 33% on the unreported gross; (b) penalty of 50% of the under-withheld tax; (c) interest; (d) the payment is disallowed as a deductible expense and taxable income is increased accordingly; (e) if the foreign shareholder is a tax evader in its home country, DIAN may also apply Article 588 of the Tax Code and publish the violation; criminal frame: if the total omitted withholding exceeds 280,000 UVT, the legal representative is exposed to 2–6 years for 'aprovechamiento de recursos' (fraudulent use of withholding characters).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the unpaid withholding (Article 403 of the Tax Code) as 'agente de retención es responsable personalmente'. If the company is dissolved, the director's liability extends to the withholding obligation as a personal debt. The director might also be penalized under Law 1065/2006 (electronic transfer of funds to a foreign recipient without justification) with a fine equal to 50% of the transfer, plus immigration restrictions on leaving Colombia until the fine is paid.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Permanent Establishment of the Foreign Shareholder (Migration to a Deemed Colombian Taxpayer)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: If the US or EU parent supplies animation projects and the Colombian S.A.S. functions as a dependent agent that habitually concludes contracts on behalf of the parent, or if the S.A.S. uses the parent's brand names and receives inbound distribution, DIAN may determine that the foreign shareholder has a permanent establishment (PE) in Colombia. For an animation service company, a PE determination arises when the Colombian headcount exceeds the parent's independent-set stage: the parent's global account manager visits the Bogotá studio, the S.A.S. issues proposals under the parent's name, and the commercial risk is borne by the foreign parent. Inbound licensing from the foreign parent to Colombian end-customers directly signed by the S.A.S. as subagent will trigger income attribution to the PE.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: If the foreign parent is deemed to have a PE, the Colombian S.A.S. becomes the PE's permanent establishment and must pay (a) 35% corporate income tax on the profits attributable to the PE; (b) the 7.5% dividend withholding on the deemed remittance to the head office (the '0.5x remittance tax' under Decree 1070/2016 is not directly applicable, but the foreign parent as a treaty-free US entity will suffer a 35% headline claim; for UK/French parents, the DTA PE threshold under Article 5 is higher but still relevant); (c) VAT on the contracts is 19% if the subsidiary is not an exporter; (d) penalties for the unregistered PE: 30% of the assessed tax and 100% of the evaded VAT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The local director of the S.A.S. may be liable as 'representante del establecimiento permanente' and thus owes the same tax, penalty, and interest; in a severe PE fraud case, criminal prosecution for 'omisión de agente retenedor' arises. In practice, given the Colombian S.A.S. is typically the contracting entity with independent authority, the PE risk is moderate, but a failure to maintain separate management minutes and board resolutions proves the dependency.
